title: NASA Vinylcals and Decals
slide_intent: Teach designers to specify an identification graphic together with its ground and measurement reference. The width of a label and the width of the printed mark describe two different products.
strategic_value: NASA can maintain legible markings on varied equipment and doors by matching the material and background to the surface.
demonstration: A rounded white vinylcal carries a red logo and black agency name. A separate decal diagram presents the logo alone. Dimension lines span the vinylcal’s white field in one example and the mark’s baseline width in the other.
practical_value: Choose the white-field label for general surfaces and the freestanding decal for a transparent surface. Specify which dimension is being measured before ordering.

content_islands.name: Identification methods
content_islands.spec: Set the section heading and introduction in the upper band. Distinguish adhesive-backed vinyl from a wet-applied decal.

content_islands.name: Vinylcal specification
content_islands.spec: Pair the upper specimen with its field-width dimension and size notes. Preserve the rounded white ground and stacked agency name.

content_islands.name: Decal specification
content_islands.spec: Place the isolated mark beneath the second divider with its baseline measurement. Keep the color, clearance and size instructions beside it.
